column1: # tools/quality/manifest.tsv -- schema v1
# The pinned source manifest for the quality analyzers. Tab-separated; '#'
# starts a comment; the first '#' line below is the column header. Read by
# scripts/install-quality-tools.sh, which verifies every value in this file and
# nothing else.
# WHAT A PIN IS HERE. `revision` is a full 40-hex commit id, never a tag and
# never a branch name. The installer fetches it with `git fetch --depth 1` and
# re-reads it with `git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD`, so the pin IS the content hash:
# it cannot move, and it is the thing that decides whether the build is the
# build this file describes.
# WHY tool_version AND compiler ARE SEPARATE COLUMNS. They answer different
# questions and conflating them produces a claim that is not true. A tool's
# `tool_version` is the version its own build.zig.zon declares; `compiler` is
# the Zig toolchain it is compiled with. zbc declares 0.1.3 and is compiled with
# Zig 0.17.0 after patch 0006. zwanzig declares 0.15.1 while its build.zig.zon still names a
# 0.15.2 minimum, because it is a dual-frontend analyzer. Neither fact is
# about the other, so neither is implied by the other.
# The patch notes below describe the historical 0001-0005 tree. Patch 0006
# ports that complete zbc tree to 0.17 without changing rules or severity.
# COLUMNS
#   id                install name; also the --only selector
#   kind              analyzer (all rows today; harness rows are not pinned here)
#   repo              clone URL. Must be one this file pins by full commit id.
#   revision          full 40-hex commit id, verified after fetch
#   revision_date     the commit's own committer date, for a human reading it
#   tool_version      the analyzer's declared version from its build.zig.zon
#   compiler          the Zig toolchain the build recipe runs
#   patches           comma-separated patch paths under tools/quality/, in apply
#                     order, or "-" for an unpatched build
#   patch_sha256      comma-separated sha256 of each patch, in the same order
#   license           license file under tools/quality/licenses/, verbatim
#   install_path      where the built artifact lands, relative to --prefix
#   build_recipe      the build step to run: a NAME, dispatched from a fixed
#                     table in scripts/install-quality-tools.sh whose only
#                     entries are `default` and `cli`. It is never eval'd,
#                     never expanded and never run as a shell command, and any
#                     other value is a manifest error, not a fallback. The
#                     installer supplies -Doptimize, --prefix and both cache
#                     directories itself and records the resolved argv per tool
#                     in install-manifest.tsv column `build_recipe`.
#                     `cli` is the named step zbc/0004 adds: it builds and
#                     installs the artifact and runs nothing else, because plain
#                     `zig build` also runs upstream's dogfood — `zbc src/` on
#                     zbc itself — which exits 1 on any finding, including the
#                     self-findings this source has about itself (75, as measured
#                     on the 0001-0003 tree; see the zbc row for what has and
#                     has not been re-measured since). `cli` is a BUILD recipe
#                     and not a lint claim: nothing here asserts the source is
#                     clean, and the default step, its install dependency and
#                     its self-check are all still there for anyone who runs
#                     them. The other three analyzers take `default`.
#   install_artifact  path inside the tool's own zig-out, relative to its root
#   source_digest     sha256 over the sorted `sha256  path` listing of
#                     src/**/*.zig, verified after patching and before cache
#                     reuse. Reproduce it with
#                       find src -name '*.zig' -type f | LC_ALL=C sort \
#                         | xargs -r sha256sum | sha256sum
#                     and a local tree that no longer matches says so.
#                     A patch that touches only build.zig cannot move it, which
#                     is why zbc/0004 leaves this column alone.
# PROVENANCE NOTES PER ROW, including what the pin does NOT establish.
#   zbc      ericsssan/zbc at 419d153 is origin/main HEAD. The upstream
#            build.zig.zon declares .minimum_zig_version 0.17.0-dev.607+456b2ec07;
#            0001 changes it to 0.16.0 together with the rest of the 0.16 port.
#            That is a source change, not a version claim, which is why the
#            compiler column exists. 0002 adds four files that do not exist
#            upstream at all. 0001 and 0002 are the two verbatim captures and
#            are left byte-for-byte untouched; together they reproduce the src
#            digest bf5331d6…c07df this file used to record. 0003 and 0004 are
#            NOT captures from anyone's working copy: both are authored against
#            the tree 0001+0002 produce, and between them they are what makes
#            that tree correct and installable, so the shipped source is
#            0001+0002+0003+0004. 0003 touches src/ only and its digest is the
#            source_digest column; it repairs three compile defects, restores the
#            double_optional_ptr rule registration 0001 deleted, restores the six
#            severities 0001 downgraded, turns SourceSelection's silent drops of
#            explicitly named inputs into reported failures, and initialises the
#            elements of a list that 0001 resized without initialising them (a
#            heap-corruption crash on every file; verified fixed by a ReleaseFast
#            build of the patched tree). One advisory severity
#            (intfromfloat_without_clamp) stays a warning by accepted, reviewed
#            policy and is disclosed in PROVENANCE.md and at the call site. Each
#            patch's own header is the full statement of that patch, including
#            one thing 0003 does NOT fix and does not hide: upstream's build.zig
#            dogfood runs `zbc src/` on every `zig build` and the CLI exits 1 on
#            ANY finding, so that self-check cannot pass for a source that has
#            findings on itself, at any severity.
#            0004 is also authored, also against that tree, and touches
#            build.zig ONLY: it names the install-artifact step and hangs a new
#            `cli` step on it, so the artifact can be built and installed
#            without the dogfood self-check, which cannot pass for this source.
#            It is that source_digest column's reason for staying put: build.zig
#            is not under src/, so the digest is b794e308…e5e3d2 before and
#            after it. What 0004 does NOT do is weaken anything: the default
#            step still installs the artifact AND still runs the self-check and
#            still fails; `zig build cli` is not a self-lint pass and no
#            severity, rule, finding or exclusion was touched to make it green.
#            The project's own gate, which runs all four analyzers and fails on
#            ERROR, is separate from both and unchanged.
#            0005 is also authored, against the tree 0001+0002+0003+0004 produce, and touches
#            src/flow/cfg_builder.zig and src/flow/worklist.zig, so this row's source_digest
#            column MOVES, from b794e308…e5e3d2 to ddcb7de4…c868, and now names 0001-0005.
#            Its full statement is its own header. In short: a false use-undefined, reported
#            on a path where a fully filling `for` body never ran — bench/bench_vec.zig
#            buildPlan and buildSeedNames were four such errors. It proves that shape from
#            the loop AST and the EXISTING FileCache .fixedArrayLenOf / .comptimeIntValueOf,
#            then emits ONE .pointer_write on the loop's exit, before any `else` is lowered
#            onto it. NO CFG EDGE TOUCHED, no `merge` clear added, emitWritesInLhs untouched,
#            no element-granular state, all 113 rules and severities unchanged, no name or
#            input special-cased, no benchmark or exported API touched. 20 tests: 4 expect no
#            findings, 16 the rule SET {use-undefined}. OBSERVED, two runs of the same
#            --test-filter "use_undefined:", 29 selected each and all passed: the first
#            BEFORE the review correction folded into the patch, the second OVER the bytes
#            as shipped, so that correction is witnessed. BUILT AND GATED: the tree
#            0001-0005 produces was built with `zig build cli`, installed into a fresh prefix
#            under an empty HOME with a REUSED work cache (so not a cold install), and the
#            full gate from that prefix is exit 0 — zbc
#            selected=32 analyzed=32 failed=0, 0 errors and the 3 standing intfromfloat
#            advisories, so the four historical bench_vec use-undefined errors are gone from
#            the project's own gate; the cross run bound to that gate reports four Linux
#            targets 348 tests each, x86_64-windows build_only.
#            NOT PROVED: no `zbc src/` self-run over 0001-0005, so its self-finding count is
#            unknown and the untouched default dogfood would still exit 1 on any finding —
#            the 75 self-findings recorded for 0003 are dated evidence about that tree, not a
#            current count; no three-run benchmark baseline, no remote GitHub Actions run and
#            no vf engine run.
#   ziglint  rockorager/ziglint at 66709a4 is origin/main HEAD, and its own
#            commit subject is "Z030: allow deinit to destroy self". One patch,
#            two files — src/Linter.zig and src/rules.zig — and NOT one rule.
#            It adds a .merge_error_sets arm to isTypeExpression (Z015 stops
#            firing on a pub fn returning a merged error set), replaces the
#            builtin-call arms of isTypeExpression and isTypeAlias with one
#            shared 14-name isBuiltinTypeConstructor predicate (Z006 stops
#            firing on @Int/@Enum/… aliases), rewrites Z030's receiver-lifetime
#            analysis and its diagnostic wording, and DELETES the eight
#            literal-message-rendering tests for Z002, Z003, Z004, Z017, Z020
#            (two), Z021 and Z030 with no replacement. Only Z030's wording
#            change requires those deletions; the rest pin exact message prose
#            rather than consumer-visible detection. They are enumerated here
#            instead of being described as one rule or as test coverage.
#   zlint    DonIsaac/zlint at 3ef67af is origin/main HEAD and is also the commit
#            tagged v0.10.0. NO PATCHES. The binary this replaces prints
#            `v0.0.0`, and that string identifies nothing: it is build.zig:329's
#            `orelse "v0.0.0"` default for the --version build option, so every
#            build from source prints it. The pin rests on fingerprints the
#            binary does expose: dependency hashes chameleon-2.0.1 and
#            smart_pointers-0.0.4 identical to the upstream zon, src/Semantic/Cfg
#            present (added 2026-08-16), and the `-c, --config` and `zlint.json`
#            help strings (added 2026-08-23 and 2026-09-15). 3ef67af is the
#            newest revision consistent with all of them. No byte-level match is
#            claimed; the installed analyzer is source-equivalent to this pin and
#            to nothing more.
#   zwanzig  forketyfork/zwanzig at 1a0768c is origin/main HEAD. It is NOT the
#            956bc69 the local checkout sits on: that commit, and the four
#            before it, appear in no origin ref of that repository, so pinning
#            them would pin something `git fetch` cannot retrieve. The five
#            local commits are therefore carried as five ordered per-commit
#            0005-956bc69), each header naming its commit and stating that it is
#            not published upstream, and the local working tree on top of them
#            is 0006-uncommitted. docs/, CHANGELOG.md, justfile, AGENTS.md,
#            CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md and .zig-cache/ from that checkout are NOT
#            archived, and neither are zbc's README.md and .github/.
# WHEN EACH PATCH WAS WRITTEN. There is no single instant for this directory
# and none is invented here; every patch states its own in its own header, and
# these are those headers transcribed.
#   zbc/0001        captured 2026-10-01T23:43:59Z from the local working copy
#   zbc/0002        captured 2026-10-01T23:43:14Z from the same copy, 45s
#                   BEFORE 0001; that is the order the tree moved in, and the
#                   reason the first zbc capture was discarded and retaken
#   zbc/0003        AUTHORED, not captured: 2026-10-02T01:28:36Z for items 1-4
#                   and 2026-10-02T04:12Z for items 5-6, both against the tree
#                   0001+0002 produce. It re-captures nothing, and no working
#                   copy, drifting or not, is its base
#   zbc/0004        AUTHORED, not captured: header records 2026-10-02T01:57Z,
#                   against the tree 0001+0002+0003 produce. The author-recorded
#                   timestamps do not establish chronology. Apply patches in
#                   numbered order.
#   zbc/0005        AUTHORED, not captured, against the tree
#                   0001+0002+0003+0004 produce. Its header records no
#                   instant, so none is recorded here either.
#   ziglint/0001    captured 2026-10-02. Its header carries a date and no
#                   instant, so none is recorded here either
#   zwanzig/0001-0005  per-commit diffs, not working-tree captures. Their
#                   headers name the commit and its subject and say nothing
#                   about when the file was written
#   zwanzig/0006    captured 2026-10-01T23:43:14Z from the local working copy
#id
